topic: Why your first page load is slow

plan.idea: Latency is distance, not bandwidth -- so you move the files closer.
plan.hook: Why is the first visit always the slow one?
plan.misconception: That a faster connection fixes a slow first load.
beats: the request chain, and what each hop costs
it is not one trip -- each file waits for the last
the obvious fix, and why it does nothing
move the destination instead of speeding up the journey
plan.payoff: Second visit is fast because nothing has to travel.

ops: text 3,2.5 "Why is the first visit always the slow one?"
say "A question with a more interesting answer than it looks."
say "Your browser asks a server, the server asks a database. Nothing exotic."
say "Notice the numbers. The hop across the ocean costs forty times the hop across the room."
text 3,22 "And that round trip only bought you the HTML."
say "Each file has to arrive before the browser knows to ask for the next one."
highlight "then JS" "By here you have paid for the crossing four times over."
say "Almost everyone reaches for this one."
strike "buy faster internet" "It does not help, and it is worth knowing why."
text 3,49 "Bandwidth is how WIDE the pipe is. This is how LONG it is."
say "A wider pipe moves more at once. It does not shorten the ocean."
note 3,64 30 "Second visit is fast because nothing travels. The files are already down the road."
say "So you do not speed up the journey. You move the destination closer."
say "That is a CDN, and that is the whole idea."
